title: Policy & Procedure for registering and admitting out-patients, in-patients and emergency patients

A.Purpose: To provide guideline instruction for admission of the patients to the inpatient care facility of the hospital.

B.Scope: This policy is applicable for indoor admission of all patients.

Abbreviations:

OP –Outpatients

OPD – Outpatient Department

IP –Inpatient patient

RC –Registration Counter

ED–Emergency Department.

EMO–Emergency Medical Officer

PV Ward– Private Ward

SPV Ward–Semi Private Ward

C.Policy:

1. IP Admission from OPD:

  • Patients visit the OP clinics of the hospital for consultation.
  • Patient assessed by the doctor in the OP clinic and decision regarding the need to admit the patient in the IP facility of the hospital is taken by the treating consultant.
  • Patients are admitted only if the required medical care is available in the hospital. In case of any discrepancy in the same, the Administrator informed by the consultant doctor for clarification.
  • The doctor informs the patient and the relatives about the need for IP admission and indicates the same in the OP case sheet of the patient.
  • The patient/relatives visit the IP registration window of the hospital for admission of the patient.
  • The patient/relative provides the OP case sheet of the patient to the admission clerk who checks the same to ensure that IP admission is advised in writing by the treating consultant of the patient.
  • The admission clerk enquires from the patient about the their preferred ward which are :
  • General Ward
  • Semi Private Ward.
  • Private Ward.

2. Admission to General Ward:

  • If the patient is to be admitted in the general wards of the hospital, the patients details as indicated in the case sheet along with the specific general ward where the patient is to be admitted is entered in the IP registration register, IP number is allotted to the patient and patients IPD FILE is prepared.
  • The IP registration fee is collected from the patient and the IPD FILE along with the payment receipt is handed over to the patient/relatives.
  • The patient visit the OP clinic of the treating consultant who examines the patient once again, writes the treatment order along with the investigation to be performed in the IPD FILE.
  • The patient along with the IPD FILE is taken to the specific ward by the ward boy who submits the IPD FILE to the respective ward nurse.
  • Patient is received in the bed by the ward nurse and made comfortable. Treatment as indicated in the IPD FILE is immediately initiated.

3. Admission to Semi Private and Private Ward:

  • If the patient is to be admitted in the semiprivate or private ward of the hospital, a separate admission form has to be filled which is available with the admission clerk in the admission window.
  • Filled in admission form along with the registration fee along with one days room rant is paid to the admission clerk.
  • Patient’s details as indicated in the admission form are filled in the designated register and an inpatient number is allotted to the patient.
  • The patients IPD FILE is prepared and handed over to the patient/relative along with the payment receipt.
  • The patient visit the OP clinic of the treating consultant who examines the patient once again, writes the treatment order along with the investigation to be performed in the IPD FILE.
  • The patient along with the IPD FILE is taken to the concerned private/semi private ward by the ward boy who submits the IPD FILE to the respective ward nurse.
  • Patient is received in the bed by the ward nurse and made comfortable. Treatment as indicated in the IPD FILE is immediately initiated.

4. Admission from ED to the IP facilities:

a. 8.00 am to 7.00 pm:

  • Patient arrives directly in the Emergency Department of the hospital.
  • The patient is immediately assessed by the ED staff. The Emergency Medical Officer attends the patient and provides immediate resuscitation.
  • In case the patient is to be seen by a specific consultant doctor for further treatment, the EMO transfer the patient to the emergency ward and the consultant doctor of the specific specialty is informed. Patients case sheet is immediately prepared.
  • The consultant doctor attends the patient in the emergency ward, examines the patient and decides whether the patient is to be admitted in the IP facilities of the hospital.
  • If the patient is to be admitted in the IP facilities of the hospital, the consultant doctor indicates the same in writing in the patient case sheet.
  • The patient/relatives visit the IP registration window of the hospital for admission of the patient.

i.If the patient is to be admitted in the general wards of the hospital ,the patients details as indicated in the case sheet along with the specific general ward where the patient is to be admitted is entered in the IP registration register , IP number is allotted to the patient and patients IPD FILE is prepared.

    • The patients IPD FILE is handed over to the patient/relatives.
    • The patient along with the IPD FILE is taken to the specific ward by the ward boy who submits the IPD FILE to the respective ward nurse.
    • Patient is received in the bed by the ward nurse and made comfortable. Treatment as indicated in the IPD FILE is immediately initiated.

ii. If the patient is to be admitted in the semiprivate or private ward of the hospital, a separate admission form has to be filled which is available with the admission clerk in the admission window.

    • Filled in admission form along with the registration fee along with one days room rent (except those mentioned below) is paid to the admission clerk.
    • Patient’s details as indicated in the admission form are filled in the designated register and an inpatient number is allotted to the patient.
    • The patients IPD FILE is prepared and handed over to the patient/relative along with the payment receipt.
    • The patient along with the IPD FILE is taken to the concerned private/semi private ward by the ward boy who submits the IPD FILE to the respective ward nurse.
    • Patient is received in the bed by the ward nurse and made comfortable. Treatment as indicated in the IPD FILE is immediately initiated.

b. After 7.00 pm till 8.00 am next morning:

  • As the OP clinic of the hospital does not function after 7.00 pm hence all patients are seen in the ED by the on duty EMO.
  • Patient arrives directly in the Emergency Department of the hospital.
  • The patient is immediately assessed by the ED staff. The Emergency Medical Officer attends the patient and provides immediate resuscitation.
  • Patient details are entered in the ED register (For ED out patients) and a case sheet is prepared.
  • If the patient is to be admitted in the IP facilities of the hospital, the EMO on duty transfer the patient to the ER ward.
  • The on call consultant of the specific specialty is informed over phone by the EMO and is briefed about the patient’s condition etc. who instructs further treatment of the patient.
  • In case the patient is serious and is to be seen immediately by the consultant doctor , the on call consultant will arrive in the hospital and examine the patient.
  • The on call consultant will decide as to whether to admit the patient in the hospital or to refer the same to the medical college for super specialty care.
  • If the patient is to be admitted, the same is indicated in the patient’s case sheet.
  • All inpatient admission after 7.00 pm is done by the ED nursing staff that follows the same procedure as indicated in the ED admissions between 8.00 am to 2.00 pm.
